figures.caption: Figure 2. Social-emotional activation within each diagnostic group. (A) [Social-emotional sentences > Reversed speech] and (B) [Social-emotional sentences > Object sentences], estimated separately in the autistic (n = 39) and non-autistic (n = 25) groups with the same model and covariates as the across-group analysis. Clusters were formed at a voxel-level threshold of p < 0.001 (t = 3.35 in the autistic group, df = 34; t = 3.55 in the non-autistic group, df = 20) and are displayed if they survived whole-brain cluster-level family-wise error correction at p < 0.05. In the autistic group no cluster survived correction for [Social-emotional > Object]; the largest sub-threshold cluster in that map (k = 117, peak t = 5.09, cluster-level p = 0.171) is reported in Table S2a. MNI z coordinates are given below each slice.
Table 2. Demographics and behavioral assessments of autistic and non-autistic children

Figure 1. Whole-brain activity across all participants (N = 64). Second-level statistical maps for (A) Reversed speech > Silence, (B) Object sentences > Reversed speech, (C) Social-emotional sentences > Reversed speech, and (D) Social-emotional sentences > Object sentences, overlaid on canonical axial slices. Clusters were formed at a voxel-level threshold of p < 0.001 (t = 3.24, df = 58) and are displayed if they survived whole-brain cluster-level family-wise error correction at p < 0.05. MNI z coordinates are given below each slice.
Table 3. Clusters and local maxima with significant activity in each contrast across all participants (N = 64).
Table 4. Group differences in region-of-interest activity between autistic and non-autistic children

Figure 3. Left superior temporal response to social-emotional sentences, and activity at the a-priori regions of interest. (A) Statistical maps for [Social-emotional > Reversed speech] and [Socialemotional > Object sentences], estimated across all participants and separately within each diagnostic group. Clusters were formed at a voxel-level threshold of p < 0.001 (t = 3.24 across groups, df = 58; t = 3.35 in the autistic group, df = 34; t = 3.55 in the non-autistic group, df = 20) and are shown if they survived whole-brain cluster-level family-wise error correction at p < 0.05. In the autistic group no cluster survived correction for [Social-emotional > Object]. White dots mark the a-priori regions of interest, labeled on the across-group surfaces: m-STS* and p-STS* are the literature coordinates of Mellem et al. (2016) and m-STS-1† and m-STS-2† are the whole-brain main-effect peaks of [Social-emotional > Reversed speech] and [Social-emotional > Object] respectively. (B) Mean contrast estimate for each group at every a-priori region of interest, extracted from a 6 mm sphere. Error bars indicate the standard error of the mean. Where the group difference was significant, the bracket gives the false-discovery-rate-corrected p value for that
